storyboard.claim: Cruz is driving far too fast in the dark before dawn.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A dark highway at dawn with Cruz holding a phone and a road icon.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cold open of the book's opening anecdote.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the speed and the speed limit so the recklessness is measurable.
storyboard.staging: Cruz looks worried while gripping his phone on the fast road.

storyboard.claim: Cruz drives straight past a marked police cruiser without noticing it.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cruz on the highway with a blank face beside the passing cruiser lane.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds that he never registered the police car at all.
storyboard.staging: Cruz stares ahead, blank, as the cruiser is passed.

storyboard.claim: Cruz has no recollection of the overtaking.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cruz with an empty expression, thinking, on the highway.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the attention lapse is total, not a choice.
storyboard.staging: Cruz sits in thought with a blank face; the lapse is the point.

storyboard.claim: A state trooper pulls Cruz over on the shoulder of Route 1 in New Jersey.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cruz on the highway shoulder, worried, as the stop happens.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The consequence of the reckless drive.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the stop on a specific road in New Jersey.
storyboard.staging: Cruz stands worried on the roadside shoulder.

storyboard.claim: Cruz's excuse to the officer is that he zoned out thinking about work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cruz, blank-faced and thinking, at the roadside window.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The explanation he gives the trooper.
storyboard.addedInformation: The excuse is absurd on its face; the blank face lets the callout carry the irony.
storyboard.staging: Cruz thinks, offering the excuse with an empty expression.

callout.text: RODE HIS BUMPER IN THE DARK

storyboard.claim: Cruz flew up behind the officer's car and practically rode its bumper in the dark.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cruz on the dark highway, worried, close behind a car.
storyboard.onScreenText: RODE HIS BUMPER IN THE DARK
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the physics of the moment.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the tailgating concrete and dangerous.
storyboard.staging: Cruz stays worried and idle while the tailgate is described.

storyboard.claim: Cruz swings out into the passing lane and keeps going.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The highway with a road icon and Cruz neutral at the wheel.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the physics of the moment.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the lane change that makes the drive dangerous.
storyboard.staging: Cruz sits neutral while the lane change is drawn.

storyboard.claim: Cruz was not drunk or drugged; he was proud of being overloaded.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cruz with a smirk, talking, at a desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Clarifies that the cause was not intoxication.
storyboard.addedInformation: The smirk shows the pride in the busyness, which is the book's target.
storyboard.staging: Cruz smirks proudly while describing his own overload.

storyboard.claim: Cruz carried a crumpled notebook page that held his to-do list.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cruz holding crumpled notes at a desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the list at the center of the story.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the list as a physical paper object.
storyboard.staging: Cruz worriedly holds the crumpled notes.

storyboard.claim: The 70-item list was crammed with two tasks per line across 35 lines.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cruz holding the notes, worried, with the list in his hand.
storyboard.addedInformation: Quantifies the crowding: two tasks per line.
storyboard.staging: Cruz holds the crowded list, worried.

storyboard.claim: The list is chaos, yet Cruz believed he was winning and the habit nearly killed him.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cruz slumped and worried at his desk.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds the stakes: the habit could kill him or someone else.
storyboard.staging: Cruz slumps, worried, under the weight of the chaos.

storyboard.claim: The list is the ultimate failure of prioritization and the core illusion about productivity.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrator voice frames the idea; no staged person.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the anecdote to the book's thesis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the central illusion of productivity.
storyboard.staging: Off-screen narration with the callout.

storyboard.claim: Cruz believed frantic exhaustion was a badge of honor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A heavy boulder beside Cruz at the desk, him smirking as if the weight were a medal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Trophy reads as a prize, matching the badge-of-honor framing.
storyboard.staging: Cruz smirks with the trophy icon as the prize he thinks he earns.

storyboard.claim: Cruz skipped lunch, ate a buttered roll one-handed while driving, and worked from before dawn to midnight.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cruz on the highway, worried, one hand on the wheel.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Continues the description of his routine.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the unsafe routine concrete.
storyboard.staging: Cruz looks worried while driving one-handed.

storyboard.claim: His overwork was not mastery but a failure of decision-making dressed up as work ethic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Cruz thinking worriedly; the callout names the failure.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The narration rejects his self-image as a master.
storyboard.addedInformation: Relabels the habit as a decision failure.
storyboard.staging: Cruz is not triumphant; he looks worried in thought.

storyboard.claim: Time management is a decision problem, not a scheduling problem.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrator voice rejects the scheduling framing; the callout is struck through.
storyboard.addedInformation: States what the book will prove.
storyboard.staging: Off-screen narrator; the struck callout carries the rejection.

storyboard.claim: The traditional approach is like packing a month-long trip into a tiny carry-on.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A professional neutral in frame with the carry-on callout.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the calendar problem as packing too much into too little space.
storyboard.staging: Everyman stands idle; the carry-on callout is the analogy.

storyboard.claim: Everything is rolled into tight tubes to fit the carry-on.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman with a warm agreeing look and the rolling callout.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the cramming visible in the analogy.
storyboard.staging: Everyman nods warmly at the analogy of rolled clothes.

storyboard.claim: Sitting on the suitcase to force the zipper shut is the picture of overpacking.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman slumped and worried with the zipper callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the suitcase image to the struggle.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the strain of cramming visible.
storyboard.staging: Everyman slumps worried as she forces the zipper.

storyboard.claim: We cram 30 hours of obligations into a 24-hour day.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman worried and thinking at a desk with the callout.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the overcommitment as a numeric gap.
storyboard.staging: Everyman thinks worriedly about the overpacked calendar.

storyboard.claim: Effective people decide to leave most of the pile behind instead of packing better.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman points as if choosing what to leave, with the callout.
storyboard.addedInformation: Quantifies the elimination at 90 percent.
storyboard.staging: Everyman points, deciding what stays behind.

storyboard.claim: Successful people eliminate rather than organize.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman points decisively with the eliminators callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names the shift from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Contrasts eliminating with organizing.
storyboard.staging: Everyman points, choosing to cut.

storyboard.claim: The study interviewed thousands of working professionals, not just read textbooks.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrator voice with the study callout.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the research was field-based.
storyboard.staging: Off-screen narration with the callout.

storyboard.claim: The study sample: seven billionaires, 13 Olympic athletes, 29 straight A students, nearly 240 entrepreneurs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A four-bucket sorter diagram of the sample groups.
storyboard.onScreenText: The sample: billionaires, Olympians, students and entrepreneurs
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the sample sizes by group.
storyboard.staging: Diagram only; narrator voice.

storyboard.claim: Mark Cuban is one of the high performers whose habits were studied.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrator voice with the Mark Cuban name callout.
storyboard.addedInformation: Adds a recognizable name to the sample.
storyboard.staging: Off-screen narration with the name callout.

storyboard.claim: Traditional time management training had zero correlation with output or reduced stress.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman with a blank look and the zero-correlation callout.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the training does not work at all.
storyboard.staging: Everyman blank: the training has no effect.

storyboard.claim: Classic time management advice is fundamentally broken, and the stakes are high for the listener.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman worried and thinking at an office desk.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows from the zero correlation finding.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the listener: a middle manager staring at an endless inbox.
storyboard.staging: Everyman worries over her inbox.

callout.text: A FAMILY CALENDAR LIKE AIR TRAFFIC

storyboard.claim: Freelancers, parents and managers all face overload; a family calendar can look like air traffic control.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman worried at the kitchen with the air-traffic callout.
storyboard.onScreenText: A FAMILY CALENDAR LIKE AIR TRAFFIC
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the parent's calendar as a concrete image.
storyboard.staging: Everyman worries at the home kitchen.

storyboard.claim: Everyone shares the same finite 1440 minutes each day.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hourglass icon with everyman and Cruz side by side.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts the audience and Cruz on one level.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the daily minute budget finite and shared.
storyboard.staging: Everyman and Cruz idle together under the hourglass.

storyboard.claim: The game is to find what successful people do differently with the same raw minutes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Narrator voice with the differently callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets the question of the episode.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the book's investigative aim.
storyboard.staging: Off-screen narration with the callout.

storyboard.claim: Successful people perceive the passage of a single minute differently, before they look at a calendar.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman thinking with the passage-of-minute callout.
storyboard.addedInformation: Locates the difference in perception, not scheduling.
storyboard.staging: Everyman thinks about how a minute is felt.

storyboard.claim: Picture a manager at a midsize company sitting at a desk.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman seated at a desk in an open-plan office.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the office scene.
storyboard.staging: Everyman sits at the desk, neutral, as the scenario starts.

storyboard.claim: The digital calendar is a solid wall of red meetings.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman seated, worried, facing a calendar in red.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the calendar density visible.
storyboard.staging: Everyman sits worried before the red calendar.

storyboard.claim: Meetings run back to back from 8:30 to 6:00 and the manager is already behind.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman slumped and worried at the desk.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the exact span of meetings.
storyboard.staging: Everyman slumps, worried, already behind.

storyboard.claim: A colleague knocks on the door frame and asks the dreaded question.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Door icon with everyman worried and thinking at the desk.
storyboard.addedInformation: The door shows the interruption coming in.
storyboard.staging: Everyman thinks worriedly as the knock comes.

storyboard.claim: Saying sure costs the manager far more than one minute.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman sad at the desk with the cost callout.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the sinking feeling of the true cost.
storyboard.staging: Everyman looks sad as she agrees.

storyboard.claim: The got-a-minute interruption never takes a minute; it is a black hole that pulls focus in.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman afraid and falling into the interruption.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the black hole a fall the viewer can read.
storyboard.staging: Everyman falls, afraid, pulled in by the interruption.

storyboard.claim: Minutes must be protected like currency from other people's urgent problems.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Shield icon with everyman pointing with the protect callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the interruption to the remedy.
storyboard.addedInformation: The shield shows protection of focus.
storyboard.staging: Everyman points, protecting her focus with the shield.

callout.text: TIME CAN NEVER BE EARNED BACK

storyboard.claim: Time is the one asset that can never be earned back.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Hourglass icon with everyman neutral and the earned-back callout.
storyboard.onScreenText: TIME CAN NEVER BE EARNED BACK
storyboard.addedInformation: States the irreversibility of time.
storyboard.staging: Everyman idle beside the hourglass.

storyboard.claim: Money, health and reputation can be recovered; time cannot.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Everyman worried and thinking with the contrast callout.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets up the word uniquely finite in the next beat.
storyboard.staging: Everyman thinks about the contrast.
